findings.text: the plan adds a create-time pending-plan census and an impl-ranked "three pending plans nearest to closing" without citing the existing readers that already compute both (reckon/roadmap.py pending_work, whose rows carry progress_pct and are sorted at reckon/roadmap.py:3142; reckon/velocity.py:408 plan_census)

findings.reason: two owners of "pending" will drift, and the gate the plan closes §3 by gates on the census the cap does not read.
findings.text: the plan's create-time count (reckon/mcp.py:3273 _pending_plans) re-derives "pending" by walking the working-tree inventory and importing only CLOSED_STATUSES, rather than consuming velocity.plan_census, the git-history census the plan's own gate g-owic-weekly-counts names as the source of pending; the two populations can disagree while the plan's done-when compares the cap against the velocity census

findings.reason: the nearest-to-closing ranking is owned by roadmap's pending-work report, so the plan should reuse its rows or justify a separate ranking.
findings.text: the "three pending plans nearest to closing, ranked by impl" (reckon/mcp.py:3294 _plans_nearest_to_closing) re-implements roadmap's pending_work rows, which already carry progress_pct per plan and are sorted by readiness/resulting priority; the plan names no owner to extend

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §3 hides the inventory walk, the closed-status definition and the impl ranking behind one project config key and one warning string, extending the create path rather than adding a plan-proposed module surface.
